hero.subtitle: Hello, I'm Zidhan. A Cybersecurity Consultant & Penetration Tester. I perform in-depth vulnerability assessments, secure web infrastructures, and help organizations maintain robust defense postures.

about.lead: I am a Cybersecurity Consultant based in Calicut, Kerala, specializing in offensive testing and vulnerability analysis.
about.bio1: Transitioning into system systems and digital defense, I leveraged my deep interest in cybersecurity to pivot into real-world application security testing.
about.bio2: To solidify my technical base, I completed a formal Ethical Hacking Diploma at the Avodha Institute in Calicut (October 2025 - April 2026), focusing on network defense systems, vulnerability analysis, and ethical hacking frameworks.
about.bio3: Today, I work as an independent consultant and security researcher, assisting organizations in identifying architectural vulnerabilities and performing responsible disclosures to secure their sensitive databases.

projects.title: E-Commerce Platform Vulnerability Assessment
projects.desc: Conducted a non-intrusive security audit on an active e-commerce application. Responsibly reported multiple vulnerabilities to help secure client networks and safeguard active transaction databases.

vulns.name: Django Debug Mode Enabled
vulns.details: Exposed internal code structures, environment keys, technical settings, database queries, and raw local variables. Exposed system paths could easily facilitate server takeovers.

vulns.name: No Rate Limiting on Admin Panel
vulns.details: The administrative login portal was completely vulnerable to rapid automated login attempts (Brute Force attacks), making default password attacks highly effective.

vulns.name: Server Software Information Disclosure
vulns.details: Server headers leaked exact software components and server versions, allowing malicious actors to target matching CVE vulnerabilities.

projects.title: Storefront Application Clickjacking Security Audit
projects.desc: Identified and verified a clickjacking (UI redirection) flaw during security research labs on an active storefront web server. Verified the bypass and responsibly coordinated a patch submission with the client.

vulns.name: Missing Frame Isolation Headers (Clickjacking)
vulns.details: The web server failed to enforce defensive boundaries, completely lacking legacy X-Frame-Options and modern Content-Security-Policy (CSP) frame-ancestors tokens. This allowed the authentication page to load inside unauthorized external frames.

vulns.name: Proof of Concept Frame Pipeline
vulns.details: Confirmed exposure by building a lightweight HTML frame wrapper that loads the user login fields inside a controlled, mock attacker-facing layer without triggering browser exceptions.
